about: The reference runs. tests/run_references.py re-runs them and compares; tests/README.md explains the fields and which checks run where. "program" is a path in the CMake build folder; each run happens in a fresh folder holding copies of "inputs" (paths in the repository). "expect" is what the run produced when it was recorded (run_references.py --record), on the machine of "machine".

machine.programs: the legacy programs (legacy/), built with the flags of their old makefiles; the runs that note says were recorded later, from the programs it names
machine.note: every run was recorded on 2026-10-25 from the legacy programs, except: three added on 2026-10-26 and recorded from the same legacy programs (byte for byte the same binaries): s4_chz5_kernel_steep, s3_zipper3_pair and s3_zipper3_pair_context; three recorded on 2026-10-26 from the new zipper5, apps/s4/zipper5, whose word reader reads facet 1: s4_zipper5_base and s4_zipper5_r18, recorded again (the legacy zipper5 drops facet 1), and s4_zipper5_t2, added; those three recorded again on 2026-10-26 from apps/s4/zipper5 with the tips (the leaves whose letter lies on a parabolic cycle of the roofs are drawn through its cusps); and the seven runs of the default files of data/, recorded on 2026-10-28 from apps/s3/zipper3 and apps/s4/zipper5 (also_recorded)

runs.title: S4: zipper5, the base arcs, accuracy 0.03, PNG 600 px
runs.note: recorded again on 2026-10-26 from apps/s4/zipper5 with the tips: each leaf whose letter lies on a parabolic cycle of the roofs is drawn through the cusp points of the cycles, exact points of the true curve (src/render/tips.h), so the spikes into the cusps reach their tips. The leaves are the same; the text has two new lines (the tips of each zipper) and ", N points at tips" in each line of the build. The picture before was base.png with SHA-256 07dc617e144a8b06d7df375a9610908913ef7587568c2d5960b1a3ecf8d573f3 (71417 bytes). Before that: recorded again on 2026-10-26 from the new zipper5, apps/s4/zipper5, whose word reader reads facet 1. The legacy zipper5 drops facet 1 from every word, so it drew this picture from misread letters, with 47 base arcs where the data have 44; that picture, the reference until then, was base.png with SHA-256 9ebed1ef59d010897f18501bd1a5d3361a047f45d542a3b843a9b0c3b2afef42 (84329 bytes). The portable pattern is the count of letters and of base arcs. --programs keeps the run as it is, since its program is already the new one.
